State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
Ajay Saini vs 1. Jain Electronics on 2 September, 2013
STATE
CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, 

 

U.T., CHANDIGARH 

 

 

 
 
 
 

First
 Appeal No. 
 
 
 

: 
 
 
 

359 of 2013 
 
 
 
 
 

Date of Institution 
 
 
 

: 
 
 
 

22.08.2013 
 
 
 
 
 

Date of Decision 
 
 
 

: 
 
 
 

02/09/2013 
 
 

 

  

 

Ajay Saini son of Sh.
Dharampal Saini, Resident of House No.1017-A, Sector 41-B, Chandigarh. 

 

  

 

Appellant/Complainant
 

 V e r s u s 

 

  

 

1.
Jain Electronics, SCO 86, Sector 40-C,
Chandigarh. 

 

2.
Carewell, Plot No. F-359, Industrial Area,
Phase 8B, Mohali. 

 

3.
Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company
Limited, Plot No.A-40, Industrial Area, Phase VIII, Mohali. 

 

  

 

 ....Respondents/Opposite Parties 

 

  

 

Appeal under
Section 15
of the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986. 

 

  

 

BEFORE: JUSTICE SHAM SUNDER (RETD.), PRESIDENT. 

 

 MR. DEV RAJ, MEMBER.
Argued by: Sh. Mohit Malik, Advocate for the appellant.
PER JUSTICE SHAM SUNDER (RETD.), PRESIDENT 

 

 This appeal is directed against
the order dated 11.07.2013, rendered by the District Consumer Disputes
Redressal Forum-I, U.T., Chandigarh (hereinafter to be called as the District
Forum only), vide which, it partly accepted the complaint, filed by the
complainant (now appellant) and directed Opposite Party No.2 (now respondent
no.2), as under:-
For the reasons
recorded above, we find merit in the complaint and the same is partly
allowed. OP-2 is directed: -
i) To handover
the washing machine to the complainant in proper working orders to his
satisfaction with a fresh warranty of one year.
ii) It is also
directed to make the payment of Rs.10,000/- to the complainant towards
harassment, mental agony on account of deficiency in service.
iii)To pay Rs.5,000/- towards litigation expenses to the
complainant.
This order shall be
complied with by OP-2 within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of
its certified copy, failing which OP-2 shall refund the amount of Rs.18,500/-
alongwith interest @9% p.a. from the date of purchase of the washing machine
till realization, apart from making the payment of compensation and
litigation.
2.     
 The complaint
against Opposite Parties No.1 and 3, was dismissed, by the District Forum.
3.     
 The facts, in
brief, are that the complainant purchased a washing machine, make GWF700 FSCPS
7.0KG, from Opposite Party No.1 authorized dealer of Godrej & Boyce
Manufacturing Company Limited/Opposite Party No.3, for a sum of Rs.18,500/- (inclusive
of VAT), on 21.03.2012, vide bill, photocopy whereof is Annexure C/1. The said washing
machine carried a warranty of 24 months, from the date of its purchase. At the
time of purchase of the said washing machine, Opposite Party No.1 assured the complainant,
that the same was of best quality, and would function properly. It was also
assured by Opposite Party No.1, that, in case of any defect, in the said washing
machine, it could be replaced with a new one, of the same description.
4.     
 After five
months of purchase of the said washing machine, the complainant noticed
inherent defects, in the same. On 19.09.2012, the complainant visited the
premises of Opposite Party No.1, with a complaint with regard to the defects,
in the washing machine. The representative of Opposite Party No.1, asked the
complainant, to visit its authorized Workshop/Service Centre i.e. Opposite
Party No.2, for rectification of defects, in the said machine. The complainant
contacted Opposite Party No.2 on 21.09.2012, which sent its representative namely
Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, to his residence. The washing machine was checked by Mr.
Sanjeev Kumar, but he was unable to
remove the defects, in the same, being beyond his reach/control, which fact was
acknowledged by him (Sanjeev Kumar), in writing, on the same day (21.09.2012).
Thereafter, on 06.11.2012, after so many complaints, one Sh.Jaswinder Singh,
came to the residence of the complainant, but he also could not find out the
defects, in the washing machine. Thereafter, various complaints were made by
the complainant, as a result whereof, on 08.11.2012, again a representative of Opposite
Party No.2, visited the residence of the complainant, and took the washing
machine with him, for rectification of defects, and a service slip, Annexure
C/2, was issued to him (complainant).
5.     
 It was
further stated that the Opposite Parties failed to refund the price of the defective
washing machine, and rectify its defects. It was further stated that no
communication was received from Opposite Party No.2, regarding the rectification
of defects, in the washing machine, which forced the complainant to buy a new one,
on 27.11.2012 vide retail invoice, copy whereof is Annexure C/3. It was further
stated that the Opposite Parties were many a time asked to redress the
grievance of the complainant, but to no avail. It was further stated that the
aforesaid acts of the Opposite Parties, amounted to deficiency, in rendering
service, as also indulgence into unfair trade practice. When the grievance of
the complainant, was not redressed, left with no alternative, a complaint under
Section 12
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (hereinafter to be called as
the Act only), was filed, directing the Opposite Parties, to refund the price
of the washing machine, lying in the workshop of Opposite Party No.2, alongwith
interest @9% p.a.; compensation, to the tune of Rs.10,000/-, for mental agony
and harassment, and cost of litigation, to the tune of Rs.7,000/-.
6.     
 Opposite
Party No.1, in its written version, admitted that it is the authorized dealer of
Godrej Electronic appliances. It was also admitted that the complainant
purchased the said washing machine, on 21.03.2012, for a sum of Rs.18,500/-. It
was also admitted that the washing machine purchased by the complainant,
carried a warranty for 24 months, from the date of its purchase, for repairs of
the product, free-of-charge. It was also admitted that the complainant
approached Opposite Party No.1, in September, 2012 and his complaint was
forwarded to the Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Limited/Opposite
Party No.3. It was stated that the complainant was also provided the address of
the authorized Workshop/Service Centre i.e. Opposite Party No.2, for redressal
of his grievance, with regard to the defects, in the washing machine. It was
further stated that the washing machine, was sold to the complainant, in intact
and packed condition. It was further stated that, after sale of the product,
Opposite Party No.1, could not be held liable, for any act and conduct of the
service provider and the manufacturer. It was further stated that neither there
was any deficiency, in rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party No.1,
nor it indulged into unfair trade practice. The remaining averments, were
denied, being wrong.
7.     
 Opposite
Party No.2, in its written version, stated that the complaint with regard to
the washing machine, was received for the first time, on 03.09.2012, regarding
vibrations in the same. It was further stated that leveling was done, in the
washing machine. It was further stated that, for the second time, the shock
absorber of the washing machine was replaced. It was further stated that the
complainant was not satisfied with the work done, on the said washing machine, and,
therefore, Opposite Party No.2, requested Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra,
Technical Department Head of Opposite Party No.3, to diagnose the defect, in
the washing machine. It was further stated that, during the checking of washing
machine by Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra,
it was found that the same was working properly. The complainant was called to
check the washing machine, thoroughly, in the workshop of Opposite Party No.2.
It was further stated that the complainant was not satisfied with the report of
Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra, in respect of the washing machine, in question. It
was further stated that the washing machine was again checked properly, at the
workshop of Opposite party No.2, and the complainant was called for delivery of
the same. Every time, future date was given by the complainant, with different
excuses that he was out of station, busy etc. It was further stated that finally,
notice of this complaint was received by Opposite Party No.2, from the District
Forum. It was further stated that the washing machine had been lying, in the
workshop of Opposite Party No.2, after thorough check up, and was in perfect
working condition, but it was the complainant, who did not turn up, to collect
the same. It was further stated that neither there was any deficiency, in
rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party No.2, nor it indulged into
unfair trade practice. The remaining averments, were denied, being wrong.
8.     
 Opposite
party No.3 in its written version, reiterated the pleas, taken up by Opposite
Party No.2, in its written version. It was stated that the complainant did not
take the delivery of the washing machine, with an intention to get undue
advantage under the Act. It was further stated that neither there was any
deficiency, in rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party No.3, nor it
indulged into unfair trade practice. The remaining averments, were denied,
being wrong.
9.     
 The Parties
led evidence, in support of their case.
10.  
 After hearing
the Counsel for the complainant, Opposite Party No.1, Sh. Raj Kumar, Manager of
Opposite Party No.2, Sh. Gangadharan, Manager Legal of Opposite Party No.3, and,
on going through the evidence, and record of the case, the District Forum,
partly accepted the complaint, in the manner, referred to, in the opening para
of the instant order.
11.  
 Feeling
aggrieved, against the non-grant of specific relief, prayed for, in the
complaint, the instant appeal, has been filed by the appellant/complainant.
12.  
 We have heard
the Counsel for the appellant, at the preliminary stage, and have gone through
the evidence, and record of the case, carefully.
13.  
 The Counsel
for the appellant/complainant, submitted that right from the day, the machine
was purchased, by the complainant, it started giving troubles. He further
submitted that the house-wife had to do the manual washing of clothes, on
account of defects, in the washing machine. He further submitted that defects,
in the washing machine, were never rectified, by the Opposite Parties. He further submitted that the washing machine
was taken to the workshop of Opposite Party No.2, which never returned the
same, after rectifying the defects therein. He further submitted that, on
account of that reason, a new washing machine had to be purchased by the
complainant. He further submitted that, as such, the complainant was entitled
to the refund of price of the washing machine, lying in the workshop of
Opposite Party No.2, alongwith compensation, but the District Forum failed to
grant the same (refund), and only granted compensation. He further submitted
that the order of the District Forum, thus, required to be modified.
14.  
 After giving
our thoughtful consideration, to the contentions, advanced by the Counsel for
the appellant, and the evidence, on record, we are of the considered opinion,
that the appeal is liable to be dismissed, at the preliminary stage, for the
reasons, to be recorded hereinafter. The purchase of washing machine, on
21.03.2012, vide retail invoice Annexure C-1, in the sum of Rs.18,500/-, by the
complainant, from Opposite Party No.1, authorized dealer of Opposite Party No.3,
was admitted. It was also admitted that the defects arose, in the machine, and
the complainant made the first complaint, on 03.09.2012, to Opposite Party
No.2. No doubt, according to Opposite Parties No.2 and 3, one Sanjeev Kumar,
Mechanic was deputed by Opposite Party No.2, who visited the residence of the
complainant for checking the same, on 21.09.2012. The washing machine was
giving noise while spinning, but Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, Mechanic of Opposite Party
No.2, could not rectify the defect. On the other hand, he told the complainant
that he will visit back, for removal of the defect. He also gave writing, on
21.09.2012, to the effect, that he could not rectify the defect, in the washing
machine, as the same was beyond his control. The affidavit of Mr. Sanjeev Kumar
was not produced by Opposite Party, to
the effect that he removed whatever defects, existed in the washing machine. Not only this, according to Opposite Party
No.2, Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra, Technical Department Head of Opposite Party
No.3, was called to diagnose the defect, in the washing machine, who visited its
(Opposite Party No.2) premises and found the same in perfect working condition.
However, the affidavit or report of Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra, Technical
Department Head of Opposite Party No.3, to this effect, was not produced, on
the record. Under these circumstances, the averments made by the complainant, to
the effect, that the defects in the washing machine were not rectified, by the
Opposite Parties, could be said to be correct. What prevented the Opposite
Parties from producing the affidavit of Sanjeev Kumar, who visited the premises
of the complainant, for rectification of defects, as also of Mr. Jaswinder
Singh Sanotra, Technical Department Head of Opposite Party No.3, who visited
the premises of Opposite Party No.2, for rectification of defects, in the said washing
machine, is not known. The District Forum was right, in holding that the
defects, occurred in the washing machine, but the same could not be rectified,
by the Mechanic and Engineer of Opposite Parties No.2 and 3.
15.  
 Ultimately,
the washing machine was taken by the representative of Opposite Party No.2, on
27.11.2012, to the workshop. According to Opposite Party No.2, after removing the
defects, in the washing machine, at its workshop, a number of calls were given
to the complainant, to pick up the same, but he put off the matter, on one
pretext or the other. However, this version of Opposite Party No.2, was also
not supported by any documentary evidence. In case, the washing machine had
been made defect free, in the workshop, then the official of Opposite Party
No.2, could write a letter to the complainant, that he should pick up the same,
as it had been made defect free. Mere oral version of Opposite Party No.2, that
the complainant was contacted, but he put off the matter, on one pretext or the
other, could not be believed. The District Forum was, thus, right in holding
that the complainant was never intimated by the official(s) of Opposite Party
No.2 that he should pick up his washing machine, as the defects therein had
been rectified.
16.  
 No doubt, in
the complaint, it was stated by the complainant that there were inherent
manufacturing defects, in the washing machine. However, no expert report was
produced by the complainant, to prove that the washing machine was suffering
from inherent manufacturing defects. In the absence of report of the expert, it
could not be said that the washing machine was suffering from inherent
manufacturing defects. Minor defects, occurring in the washing machine, during
the period of warranty, could not be
said to be inherent manufacturing defects. The District Forum was, thus, right
in holding that there was no manufacturing defect, in the washing machine.
17.  
 No doubt, the
Counsel for the complainant, submitted that since the complainant had purchased
a new washing machine, the refund of price of the machine, lying in the
workshop of Opposite Party No.2, was required to be granted by the District
Forum. The District Forum was right, in coming to the conclusion that such
submission of the Counsel for the complainant did not carry any weight,
especially, when the minor defects, in the washing machine could be rectified,
and the same could be returned to him (complainant). We also do not find any
substance, in the submission of the Counsel for the appellant/complainant, that
since the complainant had purchased a new washing machine, refund of the price
of the machine, lying, in the workshop of Opposite Party No.2, be made. The
submission of the Counsel for the appellant/complainant, in this regard, therefore,
being devoid of merit, must fail, and the same stands rejected.
18.  
 The
complainant suffered mental agony and physical harassment, on account of
defects, in the said washing machine, as after a few months of the purchase thereof,
it started giving troubles, and could not be properly used. Not only this, on
account of the fact that the washing machine has been lying in the workshop of
Opposite Party No.2, since long, the house-wife had to do the manual washing. Keeping
in view all these factors, the District Forum was right, in awarding
compensation, to the tune of Rs.10,000/-.
19.  
 The District
Forum was, thus, right in holding that there was deficiency, in rendering
service, on the part of Opposite Party No.2, in not removing the defects, in
the washing machine. The District Forum, was, also,
right in holding that Opposite Party No.2 was deficient, in rendering service,
by not sending a written notice, to the complainant, that he should take back
his washing machine, from the workshop, as the defects had been removed
therefrom, and it was in perfect working condition.
20.  
 No other
point, was urged, by the Counsel for the appellant.
21.  
 In view of the above discussion, it is held
that the order passed by the District Forum, being based on the correct
appreciation of evidence, and law, on the point, does not suffer from any
illegality or perversity, warranting the interference of this Commission.
22.  
 For the
reasons recorded above, the appeal, being devoid of merit, must fail, and the
same is dismissed, at the preliminary stage, with no order as to costs. The
order of the District Forum is upheld.
23.  
 Certified copies of this order, be sent to
the parties, free of charge.
24.  
 The file be consigned to Record Room, after
completion 

 

Pronounced.
September 2, 2013 

 

Sd/-
